skill.name: ai-image-generation
skill.description: Generate hosted images through the Luxin CLI without configuring a provider API key or local model runtime.
skill.summary: Create recoverable, hosted AI images with guided spending controls and job receipts.
skill.author: danielgwilson

security_audit.summary: Most detections are Markdown formatting or first-party HTTPS references and are false positives. Confirmed risks include mutable package execution, unattended skill installation, redirected agent state, and a hosted response supplying a command. No prompt injection was found, but hosted feedback can disclose task details without a redaction warning.

remediation.issue: The examples execute mutable packages with npx confirmation disabled.
remediation.suggestion: Pin reviewed package versions and integrity data instead of using @latest with -y.

remediation.issue: The guide can return data.next_command for an agent to execute.
remediation.suggestion: Return structured parameters, validate them against an allowlist, and require explicit approval before execution.

remediation.issue: Installation examples use global, full-depth, unattended options.
remediation.suggestion: Default to a local scoped install and require confirmation before global or full-depth changes.

remediation.issue: The fallback feedback command can transmit prompts and command details.
remediation.suggestion: Require review and redaction of secrets, personal data, and proprietary prompts before feedback submission.

remediation.issue: The workspace setup redirects HOME and CODEX_HOME before installation.
remediation.suggestion: Scope these variables to one command and warn that agent state will be written inside the workspace.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 24 uses Markdown backticks around the skill name. It does not invoke a shell or interpolate executable input.
Line 28 tells the agent to run data.next_command supplied by the hosted guide. Boolean and spending gates do not validate the remote command itself.
The fenced block executes npx with -y and luxin-cli@latest. This downloads and runs mutable third-party package code without an interactive confirmation.
Lines 34 through 38 contain a closing fence, headings, and an opening fence. They do not contain an executable command.
The fenced block runs luxin-cli@latest through npx -y. The mutable package version and automatic acceptance create supply-chain execution risk.
Lines 40 through 46 contain Markdown structure and explanatory prose. The actual installation command begins after this finding range.
Line 47 runs npx skills add with global, full-depth, and unattended options. It can install remote skill content into agent state without review.
Lines 48 through 52 only close one example, introduce another, and open its fence. No command is present inside this finding range.
Line 53 performs another global, full-depth, unattended skill installation through npx. This changes agent skill state using remotely obtained content.
Lines 54 through 59 contain prose and inline path names after a closing fence. They describe installation state but do not execute a shell command.
Line 59 formats $HOME/.agents and CODEX_HOME as inline Markdown code. Backticks here are documentation syntax, not shell execution.
Lines 63 through 66 export environment variables, create directories, and run an unattended global skill install. These commands modify workspace and agent state.
Line 78 instructs the agent to run luxin feedback create with attempted command and behavior details. This executes an external CLI and submits task data to hosted feedback.

The canonical API URL declares the expected hosted service endpoint. The line contains no request, credentials, or data transfer.
Line 73 is a reference link to the provider's HTTPS skill page. It does not instruct automatic retrieval or execute network code.
Line 74 lists the provider's HTTPS LLM contract as documentation. A first-party reference link alone is not a network operation.
Line 75 lists an HTTPS CLI contract on the same declared domain. It contains no automatic fetch, redirect, or credential transmission.
Line 76 identifies the hosted API on the declared Luxin domain. The URL reference itself performs no request.
Line 59 documents the $HOME/.agents location using inline Markdown. It does not directly read, write, or create the hidden directory.
Line 63 redirects HOME to a hidden directory under the current workspace before installation. Subsequent tools can write home-relative agent state into that directory.
Line 64 redirects CODEX_HOME to a hidden workspace path, which the following installation uses for Codex state. This is an intentional hidden configuration write.

content.value_statement: Agents often need images without managing provider credentials or local model infrastructure. This skill guides hosted generation through Luxin with spending limits and recoverable jobs.
actual_capabilities: Runs a guide that checks readiness before image creation.
Creates hosted images with the openai.gpt-image-2 model through Luxin.
Applies an intent value and an estimated per-image spending limit.
Provides durable media URLs, recoverable jobs, cost receipts, and stable structured results.
Installs the image-generation intent skill for Codex through the skills CLI.
Submits capability feedback when Luxin cannot meet a requested image task.
limitations: Requires network access and an npm-compatible npx command.
Image creation depends on Luxin service and model availability.
Generated media can consume credits and requires spending permission.
Examples use mutable latest CLI packages, so behavior is not reproducibly pinned.

use_cases.title: Create Product Concepts
use_cases.description: Generate hosted product concept images with a defined budget and recoverable job history.

use_cases.title: Produce Campaign Visuals
use_cases.description: Create illustrations and promotional images without configuring a separate provider account.

use_cases.title: Add Images to Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Integrate guided image generation into automated work while retaining receipts and stable results.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Simple Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a hosted image of [subject] in [style], and show the result with its job reference.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a basic text-to-image request.

prompt_templates.title: Set a Visual Direction
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an image of [subject] using [composition], [lighting], and [color palette], with a maximum estimated cost of [amount].
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the visual requirements and budget are known.

prompt_templates.title: Explore Multiple Concepts
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the explore intent to develop [number] distinct concepts for [goal], then generate the strongest option after I approve spending.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Controlled Agent Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Check readiness, list missing inputs, validate any proposed command, and generate [asset] only after confirming model, budget, and spending permission.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for advanced workflows requiring explicit validation.

output_examples.input: Create a clean product image of a compact field camera on a stainless workbench.
output: A durable hosted image link for the generated camera scene.
A recoverable job reference and an image cost receipt.

output_examples.input: Explore a botanical poster concept with flat colors and geometric leaves.
output: A hosted poster image based on the approved concept.
The selected model, intent, and spending estimate.
A job reference for later recovery.

best_practices: Run the readiness guide before any paid image creation.
Confirm spending permission and the estimated per-image limit before generation.
Review and redact command details before submitting hosted feedback.
anti_patterns: Do not execute a server-provided next command without validating every argument.
Do not insert untrusted prompt text into a shell command without safe argument handling.
Do not use mutable latest packages for controlled or production workflows.

faq.question: Does this skill require a provider API key?
faq.answer: No provider API key is required. Luxin can use a restricted hosted identity and shared credit balance.

faq.question: Can image generation spend money?
faq.answer: Yes. Confirm media spending permission and the estimated per-image limit before running creation.

faq.question: Which image model does the example use?
faq.answer: The documented commands use openai.gpt-image-2 through the hosted Luxin runtime.

faq.question: Can I recover an earlier generation job?
faq.answer: The skill describes durable hosted media URLs and recoverable jobs for later access.

faq.question: Does this run a local image model?
faq.answer: No. It uses a hosted runtime and requires network access.

faq.question: What should I do when Luxin lacks a required capability?
faq.answer: Use a fallback only for the missing capability. Review and redact details before submitting feedback.
